experiments.rationale: The transcript repeatedly converges from a broad blind reassignment ranking proposal to a more targeted ACA puncture challenge, and then strengthens it into the ORF-constrained ACA puncture challenge. This is presented as the highest-information next experiment because it directly tests the distinctive frozen geometry: ACA is the unique missing codon from R13 while already lying inside M13. The later turns make the proposal more concrete by requiring ORF-eligible external windows, conserved coding-context rescue for ACA->Asp, outgroup and codon-control specificity, tRNA/aaRS consistency, artifact resistance, and preservation of the median-closure invariant. The transcript states that this should be run before broad sweeps because it is targeted, externally anchored, falsifiable, and directly tests the most surprising structural feature already discovered.

Local codon-pair context lift Q^(2) explains the B*_Q6 -> protein-abundance residual that single-codon Q^(1) readouts leave irreducible: held-out 5-fold incremental Delta-R^2 of adjacent-codon synonymous B*_Q6 pair features (residualized against the 400 amino-acid-pair composition basis) exceeds the matched permutation null and clears the LAMBDA_DL complexity penalty. Tests whether the irreducible residual is local-context structure versus genuinely higher-order/non-local.

The B*_Q6 synonymous-codon residual association with yeast protein abundance is real (held-out 5-fold R^2 ~0.19 vs permutation null ~0) and partially reducible: a <=3-readout measured dictionary {measured_te, mrna_stability, turnover} captures ~24.5% of the Z-residualized abundance residual, surviving a selection-aware permutation null (null95 ~0.029, ~5x the naive fixed-subset null ~0.006); ~75% remains unexplained, and local codon-pair Q^(2) context adds no held-out signal. Certifies the residual as a real, partially-mediated (not irreducible) primitive over the tested readout family.

Hypothesis (tested, falsified): the B*_Q6 synonymous-codon residual on yeast protein abundance is an irreducible primitive -- a real held-out signal that NEITHER single-codon readout-dictionary compression NOR local codon-pair Q^(2) context captures. Result: source is real, but the {measured_te, mrna_stability, turnover} dictionary captures ~24.5% (selection-aware significant), so the residual is partially reducible, not irreducible. Explicit negative complementing the partial_mediation certificate.

A per-gene tRNA-supply readout (dos Reis tAI from yeast GtRNAdb tRNA gene-copy numbers + wobble) adds incremental held-out predictive power for Z-residualized yeast protein abundance BEYOND the measured {measured_te, mrna_stability, turnover} dictionary: 5-fold held-out delta-R^2 ~0.061 (base R^2 ~0.458 -> full ~0.519), exceeding a fixed-readout permutation null95 ~0.0007. Codon-level tRNA adaptation carries abundance information not captured by bulk measured translation efficiency, partly addressing the residual left unexplained by the partial_mediation dictionary.

Per-coordinate decomposition of the B*_Q6 -> yeast protein-abundance residual: of the 9 synonymous coordinates, 8 are real held-out abundance sources (K_AAA, Arg_AGR, Ile_AUA, Leu_CUN_vs_UUR, Leu_UUA_vs_UUG, Ser_UCR_vs_AGY, Thr_ACR_vs_ACY, f3_stress) and 1 (Ser_UCA_vs_UCG) is not; f3_stress carries the most residual energy (~20% of target, R^2~0.19) followed by Ile_AUA and Thr_ACR_vs_ACY. The measured {te,mrna_stability,turnover} dictionary's projection coverage exceeds the per-coordinate permutation null for the 8 real sources, but a large absolute residual energy remains unexplained per coordinate (e.g. f3_stress ~81% unexplained). Descriptive decomposition, not causal mediation.

The dominant B*_Q6 coordinate f3_stress (a global synonymous first-vs-last-codon direction across all 21 families) carrying ~20% of the abundance-residual energy is only MARGINALLY reachable by independent molecular measurements: the full {te,stability,turnover,localization,ptm,complex,tm,domain,mrna_abundance} readout set reaches best coverage 0.226 vs base {te,stability,turnover} 0.190 (increment +0.036, selection-aware-significant vs null95 0.027), but ~77.4% of f3_stress remains unexplained by ALL available measurements. The dominant frontier is largely orthogonal to current molecular readouts and needs new data/mechanism.

The dominant B*_Q6 coordinate f3_stress's protein-abundance contribution (P_f3, ~20% of target, ~77% orthogonal to static measured readouts) is PARTLY MEDIATED BY RIBOSOME DWELL: per-gene local ribosome occupancy features add held-out delta-R^2 ~0.019 over the {te,mrna_stability,turnover} dictionary (vs fixed-readout permutation null95 ~0.0013), and f3_stress couples positively to dwell (corr 0.162, p~8e-9, reproducing wobble-dwell). Since base already contains measured_te (footprint/mRNA), this is an increment beyond bulk TE -- a dynamic elongation mechanism partly explains f3_stress's abundance effect that static molecular readouts miss.

f3_stress's ribosome-dwell mediation of its protein-abundance contribution (P_f3) is LOCALIZED TO THE 5' TRANSLATIONAL RAMP, not the gene body: 5'-window dwell adds held-out delta-R^2 ~0.023 over {te,stability,turnover} (vs null95 ~0.0016, f3<->5'-dwell corr 0.156 p~3e-8), while 3'/body-window dwell is null (delta-R^2 ~-0.0002), and the joint 5'+3' increment ~= 5'-alone. Supports the translational-ramp hypothesis: the dominant frontier coordinate acts through slow-codon dwell at the 5' ribosome-loading region, increment beyond bulk measured_te.

Biological identity of f3_stress (the dominant B*_Q6 abundance coordinate): decomposing it into 21 synonymous family subcoordinates (exact, sum-consistency l2err~8e-16), 19/21 families are real held-out abundance sources, and the effect is DOMINATED BY GLYCINE (GGN) and ISOLEUCINE (AUU/AUC/AUA) synonymous choices (held-out R^2 0.079/0.063, energy 0.65/0.52), then Arginine (CGN, AGR), Gln, Phe, Thr, Val. So f3_stress is largely a Gly/Ile synonymous-choice axis (Ile-AUA is a known slow/wobble codon), not a uniform 'first-vs-last' artifact.

Cross-organism f3_stress->protein-abundance: the association DIRECTION generalizes near-universally (15/15 organisms held-out-significant vs permutation null after cds-length/total-codon/GC3/20-aa-composition controls, 14/15 POSITIVE; only the archaeon S. solfataricus negative), BUT the effect MAGNITUDE is strongly yeast-dominant. Held-out R^2: yeast 0.168 (clear outlier), lower-eukaryotes/some bacteria 0.01-0.05 (dicty, C.elegans, drosophila, pseudomonas, danio, bacillus), and MAMMALS negligible (human 0.0004, mouse 0.0006, rat 0.0008) -- the latter clear null only via large-n significance (explain <0.1% of variance). So the strong synonymous-codon->abundance coupling is a yeast (+lower-eukaryote/bacterial) phenomenon; in mammals the f3_stress axis is biologically negligible. NOTE: the experiment's pass gate is significance (held_out>null95), which overstates generality at large n; the honest reading is direction-universal, magnitude-yeast-dominant.

Why f3_stress is yeast-dominant: across 15 organisms its effect size = translational-selection strength x directional alignment. (1) Total synonymous-codon selection on abundance (independent 41-col full design) predicts f3 strength (Spearman rho=0.71). (2) f3_alignment sign predicts f3 direction 15/15, incl. the lone negative organism S. solfataricus (anti-aligned). Yeast is strongest because it has BY FAR the highest translational selection (syn_sel R^2=0.39, ~2x runner-up) AND positive f3 alignment (0.24). Counterexample E.coli: high selection (0.22) but f3 near-orthogonal (align 0.046) -> weak f3 (0.006), so alignment matters independently. Mammals: weak selection (0.05-0.08) -> negligible f3. So f3_stress is a 1-D proxy for the organism's codon-level translational selection; it is strong in yeast because yeast's translational selection is strongest. Caveat: n=15, no phylogenetic correction; alignment uses same-organism abundance preferences (direction-agreement partly definitional; non-circular core is the independent selection<->strength rho=0.71).

Cross-organism structure of the abundance-optimal synonymous-codon direction (15 organisms, 41-col synonymous contrast design). conservation_call=CLUSTERED: mean pairwise cosine 0.26 (not conserved>=0.6, not idiosyncratic), organized mainly by GENOMIC GC3 (GC3-delta vs cosine Pearson -0.36) more than by domain (same-domain 0.29 vs cross-domain 0.25). A weak UNIVERSAL CORE direction exists (mean held-out R^2 0.088; max yeast 0.30, E.coli 0.20). Yeast optimizes HARDEST (self-direction R^2 0.40) but in a relatively IDIOSYNCRATIC direction (core alignment 0.38, among the lowest); E.coli is core-aligned (0.77). f3_stress is a crude fixed proxy weakly aligned with everything (f3 vs core 0.26, vs yeast 0.20, vs E.coli 0.22). Caveat: n=15, no phylogenetic correction, optimal direction inferred from abundance-associated contrasts (not causal).

Window6 boundary set R biological-signature test (bridge BC1 empirical contact). The 10 R sense-codons (math/geometry-derived boundary, NO usage fitting) are systematically AVOIDED (lower abundance-preference than non-R sense codons) in ALL 15/15 organisms (cross-organism sign test ~ p 6e-5), but only 6/15 reach individual per-organism permutation significance, so the experiment's strict gate (>=8 significant) emits FAILED. Honest reading: the abstract Window6 boundary R HAS a real, directionally-universal biological signature (it is the set of avoided codons), under-detected by the per-organism gate (small-genome power). Same pattern as f3 cross-organism (direction universal, per-organism magnitude varies). Supports BC1's empirical prong; the math forcing prong still pending. Follow-on: a cross-organism sign-test gate would call this supported.

Mechanism for why Window6 boundary set R is biologically avoided (Route L): the 10 R sense-codons are systematically tRNA-POOR (lower dos-Reis tAI weight, from GtRNAdb tGCN+wobble) than non-R sense codons in 31/40 organisms (cross-organism sign test binomial two-sided p~7e-4; 9/40 opposite, so predominant not universal). So the math-defined Window6 boundary R = the translationally non-optimal / tRNA-scarce codons -> they are decoded slowly and selected against -> avoided (Route L). Gives the abstract boundary a real mechanistic biological identity. Deterministic; tAI from GtRNAdb. Caveat: tAI is a supply proxy, not direct decoding-rate; 40 organisms no phylogenetic correction.

Route N: the cross-organism universal optimal synonymous-codon direction (the weak universal core of Route K) is substantially the tRNA-adaptation direction. Across 11 organisms with both proteomes and GtRNAdb tRNA-gene copies, each organism's abundance-optimal direction (full 41-dim synonymous contrast) aligns with its dos-Reis tAI tRNA-supply direction at mean cos 0.267 (median 0.302; cross-organism sign test 10/11 positive, p~5.9e-3; normal-approx p~7e-7), and the tRNA direction ALONE recovers ~43% (pooled held-out R2 ratio 0.434; median per-organism 0.30) of the abundance signal the full optimal direction captures (mean tRNA-alone held-out R2=0.059 vs self R2=0.136). The tRNA direction also aligns with the cross-organism universal core at cos 0.246 (9/11 positive, p~0.033). So translational selection toward tRNA-abundant codons is a MAJOR but PARTIAL (~43%) component of universal codon optimality, not the whole thing -- consistent with f3 residual dominance and the ~24.5% reducibility of B*_Q6. Deterministic; tAI from GtRNAdb tGCN+wobble. Caveat: 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb), tAI is a supply proxy not a direct decoding rate, no phylogenetic correction.

Route O: the NON-tRNA component of universal codon optimality is the f3-stress translational-selection axis, NOT GC mutational bias. After Gram-Schmidt-removing each organism's tRNA-adaptation direction from its 41-dim abundance-optimal synonymous direction (Route N), the residual aligns with the f3-stress axis (mean cos 0.139, 10/11 organisms positive, cross-organism sign-test p~5.9e-3, normal-approx p~6e-6) and is ANTI-aligned with the GC3 mutational-bias axis (mean cos -0.073, 10/11 negative). The GC3 and f3-stress reference directions are nearly anti-parallel in this contrast space (cos -0.905), so the residual selects the f3/translational-selection pole over the GC/mutation pole (paired |cos_f3|>|cos_gc| in 11/11 organisms, p~4.9e-4). Combined with Route N (~43% tRNA-adaptation), B*_Q6 codon optimality decomposes into TWO translational-selection mechanisms -- tRNA-supply adaptation + f3-ramp stress -- with GC mutational bias as the opposite pole, not a positive driver. Deterministic; 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb). Caveat: f3 cosine magnitude is modest (0.139) though directionally consistent; GC/f3 near-antiparallel means the two readouts are not independent; observational not causal; E.coli/P.aeruginosa/etc lack GtRNAdb (needs_data); no phylogenetic correction.

Route P: universal codon optimality is NOT 2-dimensional (tRNA + f3) -- a universal THIRD selection axis exists. Projecting each organism's 41-dim abundance-optimal synonymous direction onto span{d_tRNA, d_f3} captures only mean 13.0% of its norm^2 (captured_fraction mean 0.130, median 0.102, 11/11 organisms < 0.5); the residual-after-both direction d_perp retains ~93% of the optimal norm. d_perp is NOT noise: systematically positive held-out R2 (mean 0.066, 11/11 positive, p~4.9e-4) recovering ~64% of the self-direction abundance R2 (d_perp/self ratio mean 0.640), and CROSS-ORGANISM ALIGNED (55-pair mean cosine 0.179, 38/55 positive, sign-test p~3.2e-3, normal-approx p~1.6e-6). In 8/11 organisms d_perp alone out-predicts the tRNA+f3 plane combined (two-axis recovers ~40% of self R2). So codon optimality has at least THREE universal selection dimensions; tRNA-supply adaptation (Route N) + f3-stress (Route O) are real but together a MINORITY of the optimal direction's geometry and predictive content. The identity of the third universal axis d_perp is the open frontier. Deterministic; 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb). Caveat: cosines modest; observational not causal; no phylogenetic correction; d_perp is an orthogonal-complement residual so its mechanistic identity needs separate characterization.

Route Q: the third universal codon-optimality axis d_perp (Route P) is provisionally identified as the within-synonymous-family USAGE-FREQUENCY axis (preferred-codon bias). Across 11 organisms d_perp aligns with the within-family usage-frequency direction at mean cos 0.128 (11/11 organisms positive, cross-organism sign-test p~4.9e-4) -- the ONLY tested candidate axis clearing the cross-organism gate. Other candidates are weak/non-significant: position composition (pos3_C 0.084 7/11 ns, pos1_C 0.079 8/11 ns), residual GC3 (0.054 9/11 p~0.03 marginal), the other 8 B*_Q6 synonymous coordinates, amino-acid/position composites -- none explain d_perp. So codon optimality has THREE universal selection axes: tRNA-supply adaptation (Route N), f3-stress 5'-ramp translational selection (Route O), and the genome-wide preferred-codon usage-frequency bias (Route Q), the last distinct from tRNA-supply. Deterministic; 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb). Caveat: cosine modest (0.128); usage-frequency correlates with expression so part of this reflects the abundance-optimal direction recovering the preferred-codon set, and the deeper driver of usage-frequency beyond tRNA is itself composite/open; observational; no phylogenetic correction. Also exports per-codon d_perp + tRNA-supply vectors in the codon-Q6 6-bit frame (codon_q6_selection_vectors.json) fulfilling the Window6-codon bridge BC5 data request.

Route R: the third universal codon-optimality axis d_perp (Route P/Q, the within-family preferred-codon/usage-frequency direction) is a GENUINE cross-organism SELECTION signal -- NOT a GC/mutational projection and NOT the wobble-decoding axis. GC-null defeat: after orthogonalizing d_perp against the GC3 direction it remains cross-organism aligned (55-pair mean cosine 0.177, 38/55 positive, sign-test p~3.2e-3) and still predicts protein abundance held-out (mean R2 0.071, 11/11 positive, p~5e-4) -- essentially unchanged from pre-orthogonalization (0.179/0.066); GC3 alone gives only R2 0.028. So d_perp is not mutational GC bias. Wobble test: d_perp per-codon loadings do NOT cluster by wobble-decoding class (exact-match vs wobble, NNU/NNC vs NNA/NNG, 2-codon U/C splits) -- not the tRNA-modification/wobble axis. The leading remaining identity -- CSC / mRNA-stability codon optimality (codon-mediated decay) and 5'-vs-CDS-body positional localization -- requires external data (published CSC vectors / mRNA half-lives / positional CDS) and is flagged needs_external (repo holds only whole-CDS codon counts). Deterministic; 11 organisms. Net: the third optimality axis is a real preferred-codon SELECTION pressure distinct from tRNA-supply, the 5'-ramp f3 axis, GC mutation, and wobble decoding; most plausibly mRNA-stability-driven, pending external CSC/half-life data. Oracle (chatgpt-pro) independently ranked CSC/mRNA-stability as the #1 candidate.

Route S (optimality-axis sufficiency, independent-axis design): the three NAMED mechanistic codon-optimality axes -- tRNA-supply (tAI), f3-ramp, within-family usage-frequency -- are NOT sufficient to explain the universal abundance-optimal direction. Using axes each defined INDEPENDENTLY of the optimal direction (anti-circularity sanity captured_fraction<1 enforced), the three jointly span only ~16.4% of the optimal direction's norm (captured_fraction_3indep 0.164 vs 0.130 for tRNA+f3 alone; usage-frequency adds only ~3.4% geometric) and recover ~45% of held-out abundance R2 (three-axis/self R2 0.448 vs 0.395 for two axes). A FOURTH universal mechanism remains: the residual d_resid4 (d_opt minus the 3 independent axes) is cross-organism ALIGNED (55-pair mean cosine 0.172, 38/55 positive, sign-test p~3.2e-3) and recovers ~56% of self-optimal abundance R2 (mean R2 0.058, 11/11 positive) -- the majority of the universal codon-optimality signal lies OUTSIDE the three identified mechanisms and is still unidentified. So codon abundance-optimality is at least 4-dimensional. CORRECTION NOTE: an earlier residual-basis design gave captured=1.0 ('three axes sufficient') tautologically because the third axis was defined as d_opt's own residual; this independent-axis design (tAI/f3/usage all from biology, not from d_opt) avoids that circularity. Deterministic; 11 organisms. Caveat: d_resid4 held-out R2 carries the usual full-sample-direction optimistic bias, but the cross-organism cosine alignment and the captured-fraction are bias-free; observational; no phylogenetic correction.

Route T (per-organism axis-strength spectrum): across all 11 organisms the captured-fraction spectrum of codon abundance-optimality is dominated by the unidentified 4th component d_resid4 (dominant axis in 11/11 organisms), d_tRNA second, f3 and usage-frequency secondary. NO organism is primarily explained by the named tRNA/f3/usage axes -- the unidentified mechanism leads universally. (Honest note: d_resid4's captured dominance is the geometric complement of the 3-named-axis ~16% capture from Route S, so this is a per-organism RESTATEMENT of Route S, not an independent finding; the genuinely new content is the per-organism universality and the domain/GC nulls below.) Cross-domain structure: NOT detectable -- domain means are descriptive only under imbalanced n (archaea 1, bacteria 2, eukaryote 8), low power; no significant domain difference in the spectrum. Genome-GC covariation: only the usage-frequency axis weakly tracks GC3 (Spearman rho 0.136). Deterministic; 11 organisms. So identifying the dominant 4th mechanism (most plausibly CSC/mRNA-stability, needs external data) is the key open frontier; the named-axis mix does not vary detectably by domain at this sample size.

Route U: the unidentified 4th universal codon abundance-optimality axis (d_resid4, Route S/T) is NOT mRNA-stability/CSC -- refuting the leading hypothesis (oracle-ranked #1). Using in-repo per-gene mRNA-half-life data (yeast Neymotin + E.coli + human; NOT external), the half-life-optimal codon direction aligns only weakly with d_resid4 (cos 0.098) and more with tRNA (0.223)/usage (0.163); half-life optimality is itself barely in the named-axis span (captured 0.062). POSITIVE narrowing: the 4th axis IS shared across the abundance / translation-efficiency / mRNA-level optimal directions (TE-opt . d_resid4 = 0.616, mRNA-level-opt . d_resid4 = 0.544) but NOT half-life (0.098) -- so the dominant 4th mechanism is an EXPRESSION/TRANSLATION-level codon optimality common to abundance+TE+mRNA-abundance, distinct from mRNA-decay/stability. Caveat: the three named axes are geometrically correlated (f3-usage cos 0.711, tRNA-usage 0.499) despite independent biological definitions, so the 'span' overlaps; yeast-primary (half-life/TE richest there), cross-organism limited; cross-readout cosines are bias-free but held-out R2 carries the full-sample-direction optimistic bias; observational, no phylogenetic correction. Net: the 4th mechanism stays unidentified but is constrained -- NOT mRNA-stability, IS a shared expression/translation-level axis.

Route V: the dominant 4th universal codon-optimality axis is NOT codon-pair bias (refuting oracle #5, after Route U refuted #1 mRNA-stability). Per-gene codon-pair-bias (Coleman obs/exp adjacent in-frame pairs, in-repo ordered CDS seqs, yeast 5810 + E.coli 3738 genes) adds ZERO held-out abundance increment beyond the single-codon three axes (yeast increment R2 -1.8e-5; 3-axis+CPB 0.3077 ~ baseline 0.3077; codon-shuffle null p=1.0). CPB single-codon marginal does NOT align with d_resid4 (cos -0.23 yeast, |cos| 0.27 E.coli) and is largely just usage (|cos| d_usage 0.68 E.coli). Deterministic; yeast+E.coli. NET 4th-mechanism elimination: NOT mRNA-stability (U), NOT codon-pair (V), NOT wobble (R), NOT GC (R); specific identity unresolved with current repo data (remaining: co-translational elongation/ribosome-dwell, 5'-structure -- need dwell/structure data not cleanly available).

Route W: ribosome-dwell/elongation is NOT the unidentified 4th codon-optimality axis (partial verdict). The per-codon ribosome-dwell direction (yeast riboseq positional occupancy, 1.41M windows, synonymous-contrast encoded) aligns with the 4th residual d_resid4 only cos -0.095, but aligns strongly with the already-NAMED axes: usage cos 0.640, tRNA 0.323, f3 0.272. So ribosome-dwell IS a real codon-optimality signal but it is the named-axes bundle (mostly usage-frequency), NOT the missing 4th residual. Deterministic; yeast-only (riboseq occupancy single-species -> no cross-species power). This COMPLETES the 4th-mechanism elimination over all repo-testable candidates: the dominant unidentified 4th expression/translation-level axis is NOT mRNA-stability (U), codon-pair (V), wobble-decoding (R), GC/mutation (R), or ribosome-dwell/elongation (W). ARC CONCLUSION (Route N->W): codon abundance-optimality is >=4-dimensional; the three named selection axes (tRNA-supply + f3-ramp + usage-frequency) capture only ~16% of the optimal direction's geometry, and the dominant cross-organism-universal residual axis is real but mechanistically OPEN -- not explained by any standard single-codon mechanism with currently-available data.

Route X (translation->protein-localization boundary, first protein-PHENOTYPE-layer test beyond abundance): B*_Q6 does NOT robustly cross the translation->subcellular-localization layer -- its apparent localization discrimination is largely protein-composition/length-confounded. Held-out multiclass localization discrimination (yeast 4304 / human 10187 / danio 1908 genes): B*_Q6 beats baseline (Δacc +0.022, Δmacro-AUC +0.078) and SURVIVES translation controls (abundance+TE; Δacc +0.023, ΔAUC +0.021), BUT collapses to ~0 after additionally controlling protein length + amino-acid composition + GC (cross-organism aggregate Δacc -1e-5, ΔAUC -0.0014). Only yeast retains a weak per-organism full-control residual; human and danio are partial and the aggregate full-control increment is null -> NOT replicated. So the codon-Q6 signal carries no localization information independent of protein composition/length; the apparent codon->localization channel is a composition confound (verdict: partial, leaning blocked_null). Deterministic; yeast+human+danio. Anti-over-claim: the per-organism 'crosses' for yeast was downgraded to partial at the headline (orchestrator-fixed verdict gate) because the cross-organism aggregate increment does not survive length+aa+GC controls. Caveat: multi-label localization reduced to primary classes; 3 organisms; held-out CV.

Route X2 (translation->protein-stability boundary): B*_Q6 does NOT independently cross to the protein-stability layer -- same composition-confound pattern as localization (Route X). Across 3 organisms (yeast/E.coli/human, 12751 genes), B*_Q6 predicts protein/mRNA stability (Δr2 +0.028 vs baseline, 3/3 positive) and weakly survives translation controls (Δr2 +0.010, 2/3), but the FULL-control increment (translation+length+aa+GC) collapses to -0.0026 (1/3 positive), indistinguishable from the sign-flip permutation null (null mean -0.0028; p(obs>0)=0.95). So the codon-Q6 stability signal is fully explained by protein composition/length; no independent stability information (verdict partial, leaning blocked_null). EMERGING BOUNDARY (with Route X localization): the codon-Q6 channel reaches protein ABUNDANCE (the N->W optimality arc) but does NOT independently cross to downstream protein phenotypes (localization, stability) -- those apparent signals are protein-composition/length confounds. Deterministic; 3 organisms; held-out CV + sign-flip null + full composition controls.

Route X3 (translation->protein-structural-order boundary): B*_Q6 DOES independently cross to the protein structural-order layer -- the one downstream phenotype (of those tested) where the codon signal survives full controls, consistent with co-translational folding. Across yeast + E.coli (2/2 organisms, both domains), B*_Q6 predicts protein structural order/disorder (Δr2 +0.099 vs baseline) and the increment SURVIVES the full controls (translation+length+aa+GC): full-control Δr2 +0.0053 (2/2 positive), above the sign-flip permutation null (null -0.0021; p(obs>0)=0.0029). Unlike localization (Route X) and stability (Route X2) -- which collapsed to the composition null -- structural order retains a small (~0.5% incremental R2) but REAL, composition-independent, cross-domain-replicated codon signal. Mechanism consistent with co-translational folding (local codon usage tuning elongation rate to aid folding/disorder). Deterministic; 2 organisms (yeast+E.coli); held-out CV + sign-flip null + full composition controls. Caveat: small magnitude; only 2 organisms; per-protein order/disorder readout. PROTEIN-PHENOTYPE BOUNDARY MAP (Route X/X2/X3): codon-Q6 crosses to ABUNDANCE (strong, optimality arc) and STRUCTURAL ORDER (small, co-translational folding) but NOT to localization or stability (composition confounds).

Route X3b (structural-order crossing axis identity): the codon-Q6 -> protein-structural-order crossing (Route X3) is carried predominantly by the f3_stress (5'-ramp) axis -- confirming the co-translational folding mechanism. Of the 9 B*_Q6 coordinates, f3_stress is the ONLY individually-significant carrier of the full-control structural-order increment (weighted held-out Δr2 +0.0032, sign-flip p=0.031, 2/2 organisms), accounting for the bulk of the full B*_Q6 increment (+0.0038, p=0.017); all other axes are individually non-significant (Arg_AGR p=0.14, Ile_AUA p=0.069, ...). So the same 5'-ramp translational-selection axis (f3_stress) that dominates abundance-optimality (Route O) is ALSO the axis that reaches protein structural order -- one elongation/ramp axis spanning both abundance and co-translational folding. Deterministic; yeast+E.coli. Caveat: f3_stress p=0.031 (modest), 2 organisms; per-organism dominant LOADING varies (yeast K_AAA, E.coli f3_stress) but the increment-based ranking puts f3_stress uniquely significant. CLOSES the protein-phenotype boundary arc (Route X/X2/X3/X3b): codon-Q6 crosses to abundance + structural-order (both via the f3/ramp co-translational-selection axis), not to localization or stability (composition confounds).

Route Y (4th-mechanism candidate: translation accuracy): the dominant unidentified 4th codon-optimality axis is NOT translation-accuracy / near-cognate mistranslation-robustness either (oracle's top remaining bet, refuted). Per-codon Accuracy score = log(cognate dos-Reis decoding supply / one-mismatch missense near-cognate pressure x Grantham severity), residualized against {tAI,f3,usage,GC,wobble} + within-family centered, tested across 11 organisms with 3 oracle-designed gates -- ALL 3 FAILED: (a) codon-axis alignment with d_resid4: median abs cosine 0.07, within-family permutation null median p=0.71 (NS; 8/11 same sign but only drosophila/yeast individually significant); (b) gene held-out abundance increment beyond known axes: mean Δr2 +0.0043, sign-test p=0.11 (NS); (c) structural-order gradient: only yeast has data and accuracy is stronger in DISORDERED (Δ +0.023) than ordered (Δ +0.0036) regions -- OPPOSITE the co-translational prediction. ELIMINATION LEDGER (4th universal optimality axis): NOT mRNA-stability, codon-pair, wobble, GC, ribosome-dwell, OR translation-accuracy -- 6 standard codon-bias mechanisms excluded. The dominant cross-organism-universal optimality axis remains a genuine open mystery, resistant to standard single-mechanism explanation with available data. Deterministic; 11 organisms; permutation null + full controls; codex verdict conservative/correct (0/3 gates passed, no over-claim).

Route Z (f3-ramp evolutionary portability, oracle-proposed genuinely-new direction): tests whether within-orthogroup cross-species differences in the 5'-ramp f3 signal predict conserved same-direction differences in protein abundance/TE/structural-order (ortholog + species fixed effects, controlling aa-composition/GC/tRNA/length; negative controls half-life/localization). NEEDS_EXTERNAL with current repo data: no species pair satisfies BOTH (enough 1:1 orthologs) AND (full features both sides). Attempt 1 yeast+human: human lacks ordered-CDS + structural-order locally. Attempt 2 yeast+E.coli (cross-domain): a real OrthoDB fetch ran (598/600 requests, 474s, not rate-limited) but found 0 exact local 1:1 orthogroups with full features among 352 orthogroups seen -- cross-domain (eukaryote vs bacteria) 1:1 orthology + full-feature coverage is too sparse. So the portability question is feasible IN PRINCIPLE (OrthoDB reachable) but blocked on data: needs human ordered-CDS+structural-order or >=3 same-kingdom full-feature species. Honestly registered needs_data (data gap documented); NOT a scientific verdict. Local feature coverage confirmed: yeast 5810 genes (abundance+TE 5128+structural 5804+half-life 5379+localization 4831), E.coli 3738 (abundance+TE 3415+structural 3736+half-life 2947; no localization).

Route X3c (positional/ramp localization of the f3->structural-order crossing): the f3->structural-order signal (Route X3) is RAMP-CONCENTRATED, consistent with co-translational folding, though ramp-exclusivity is only marginally significant at 2 organisms. At the first 50 codons, ramp f3 crosses to structural order (held-out Δr2 +0.0011, sign-flip p=0.048, 2/2 organisms yeast+E.coli) while CDS-body f3 does NOT (Δr2 -0.0003, p=0.54, 0/2); ramp > body in 2/2 organisms (paired Δr2 +0.0014, paired sign-flip p=0.059 -- just above 0.05). So the structural-order crossing is driven by the N-terminal ramp window, not the CDS body -- the per-arm pattern (ramp significant, body NS, ramp>body 2/2) supports the co-translational-folding spatial prediction, but the strict ramp-vs-body paired test is marginal (underpowered at 2 organisms; codex conservatively labelled 'ramp_positive_but_not_localized' because the paired gate p=0.059 narrowly missed 0.05). N=30 sensitivity weaker (ramp p=0.30); the effect emerges at a ~50-codon window. Deterministic; yeast+E.coli; held-out + sign-flip null. Completes the f3->structural-order mechanism line (X3 crossing / X3b f3-axis carrier / X3c ramp-concentrated): a 5'-ramp f3 co-translational-folding channel, modest and marginal but directionally coherent.

experiments.statement: A frozen internal codon-coordinate used only as a design axis is tested against matched synonymous ADAR A-to-I editing loss/rescue data at the RNA level.
experiments.rationale: Across the consultation, several external layers were proposed, but the strongest clean failure test was explicitly identified as the ADAR-mediated A-to-I RNA-editing bridge. It offers a sharp collapse criterion: if ADAR loss or catalytic inhibition removes the Q-associated editing difference and wild-type ADAR rescue restores it, while catalytic-dead or binding-defective rescue fails, the external readout is tied to a measured, perturbable biological bridge. If the editing effect instead follows RNA structure or local dsRNA substrate strength better than ADAR occupancy, the mechanism claim fails and must be rescoped.
